newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends broadly higher, funds buy.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends broadly higher, funds buy.

text.p: CSCE world sugar prices ended broadly higher Friday, fueled by heavy fund buying in the nearby months, traders said.

Interest focused on the nearby May-July switch at the outset, as speculators squared books ahead of the weekend. Commodity funds raced to buy the market once July cleared the widely-watched 11.00 cent barrier, driving prices to a one-week high.
Some producer-linked selling emerged at the highs, helping to pare the day's gains by the close.
Benchmark July futures rose 0.21 cent a lb, to close at 11.09 cents, after touching a high of 11.18 cents. The spot May contract rallied 0.33 cent, to 11.29.
Traders said talk that Russia was an interested buyer also lent the market impetus, though no deals were confirmed.
On the charts, today's breach of 11.00 cents was seen as technically constructive, though the 11.18 mark would remain a tough hurdle, traders said.
"I would not be surprised to see the market trade 20 points higher," said one broker. Support was noted at 11.00 cents, followed by 10.87 and 10.77-10.78.
The day's volume was heavy, at an estimated 43,366 lots.
((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
